question: What universal maximum service life, in years, does the MUTCD assign to every traffic sign before mandatory replacement?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not assign any universal maximum service life, in years, to traffic signs, and none of the evidence provided contains such a provision. Sign replacement in the MUTCD is governed by condition-based criteria (such as maintaining legibility and minimum retroreflectivity), not by a fixed age limit. The premise of the question is not supported by the evidence, so no year figure can be cited. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2H-1, which lists general information sign and plaque sizes, not service life. [Image 2] shows Figure 2A-2 with sign mounting heights and lateral offsets, not replacement intervals. [Image 3] shows Figure 2A-3 with sign locations at intersections, not service life. [Image 4] shows Figure 2A-4 relating to sign location, not replacement. [Image 5], [Image 6], [Image 7], and [Image 8] show table-of-contents and sign-design pages with no mention of a mandatory replacement age. Citations: - Table 2H-1 (p.460) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Figure 2A-4 (p.50)
